query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor microalloying addition that promotes in‐situ nanoprecipitate formation in the CoCrFeNi matrix will create a nanohierarchical architecture that enables adaptive friction interface protection, thereby maintaining a low coefficient of friction and ultralow wear rate from room temperature up to 800 °C.
generation.material_initial_state: A homogeneous CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy lacking distinct nanoscale precipitates or composition undulation.
generation.intervention: Add a small percentage of elements (e.g., Al, Nb, Ti, V) that are known to form nanoprecipitates, triggering a nanohierarchical architecture during sliding at elevated temperatures.
generation.conditions: Sliding tests performed under identical loads and speeds in a dry or minimally oxidizing environment over a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: A nanohierarchical microstructure characterized by coupled nanoscale grains and well-distributed nanoprecipitates leading to composition undulation.
generation.mechanism: At lower temperatures, the nanoprecipitates help distribute frictional stress through multiple deformation pathways, while at higher temperatures the architecture promotes the formation of a dense, nanocrystalline glaze layer that minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy, the microalloyed variant is expected to display a substantially reduced wear rate (potentially in the order of 10⁻⁷ to 10⁻⁶ mm³/Nm) and maintain a low coefficient of friction consistently across the entire temperature range.
generation.baseline: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with a uniform, single-phase microstructure and no adaptive nanostructure.
generation.boundary: Performance evaluation under sliding conditions across 25 °C to 800 °C with load and speed parameters similar to established tribological test protocols; the environment should mimic low-oxidation conditions to reduce extraneous effects.
generation.uncertainty: The extent of microstructural evolution under dynamic sliding conditions and the quantitative improvement in wear resistance is uncertain until experimental validation is performed.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of baseline CoCrFeNi alloy and another of the CoCrFeNi alloy microalloyed with precipitate-forming elements. Conduct sliding wear tests under identical load, speed, and environmental conditions while gradually increasing the temperature from room temperature to 800 °C. Post-test, perform microstructural analyses (TEM/SEM, XRD) to verify the presence of the nanohierarchical architecture and associated nanoprecipitates.
measurements: Wear rates using profilometry or mass loss measurements
Coefficient of friction during sliding tests
Phase and composition analysis using XRD and EDS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the microalloyed samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in wear rate and coefficient of friction across the temperature range compared to the baseline, or if the anticipated nanohierarchical structure and nanoprecipitates are not confirmed by post-test microstructural analyses, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Remarkable Wear Resistance in a Complex Concentrated Alloy with Nanohierarchical Architecture and Composition Undulation

Abstract: AbstractSustained wear damages on the sliding surfaces of alloys are generally the culprit responsible for the failure of various mechanical systems. Inspired by high-entropy effects, here we deliberately deploy nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation in a Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 complex concentrated alloy, which yields ultralow wear rate within the order of 10−7 to 10−6 mm3/Nm between room temperature and 800 °C. Such remarkable wear resistance heretofore represents one of the highest wear resistance reported for the bulk alloys or composites, and originates from the multi-type adaptive friction interface protection governed by intrinsically nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates. This cooperative heterostructure releases gradient frictional stress in stages upon wear at room temperature through the coexistence of multiple deformation pathways while activating a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer upon wear at 800 °C to minimize adhesive and oxidative wear.
